knowledge_point.title: Calculating an Angle or Side of a Triangle Given the Area of a Triangle

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105904/plots/dd239ae74386e8d5e2aa263c4fce5d4ed76a158e79559a03e85a079fc9c03410.png)

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $6cm^{2}$. Find $AC$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=12\text{ cm} \\ b & =AC \\ m∠A & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{1}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 6 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 12\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\ 6 & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 12\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\ 6 & =3b \\ b & =\frac{6}{3} \\ b & =2\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=2\,\text{cm}.$

The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105904/plots/4a87803468f20552cbc4c032ddba879ba9c0b21594166a15b0658e63a1a2d1f3.png)

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{21\sqrt{2}}{8}{\text{ cm}}^{2}.$ Find $AC.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=3\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={45}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{8} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 3\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{45}^{∘} \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{8} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 3\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{21\sqrt{2}}{8} & =\frac{\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\,b}{2} \\ \frac{\frac{21}{4}\cancel{\sqrt{2}}}{\cancel{2}} & =\frac{\frac{3}{2}\cancel{\sqrt{2}}\,b}{\cancel{2}} \\ \frac{3}{2}b & =\frac{21}{4} \\ b & =\frac{7}{2}\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=\frac{7}{2}\,\text{cm}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105904/plots/6d5ddffe5fa0336a4db0c7d07f34bf311e8ac4aa24ce2b8d85ecf122c9a2c20d.png)

The area of the triangle $△ABC$ is $\frac{35}{2}\,\text{mm}^{2}.$ Use $\sin30^{\circ}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Then, $AC=${{field-1}} $\text{mm}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=7\text{ mm} \\ b & =AC \\ m∠A & ={30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}=\frac{1}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ \frac{35}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘} \\ \frac{35}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 7\cdot (\frac{1}{2}) \\ \frac{35}{2} & =\frac{7}{4}b \\ b & =\frac{\frac{35}{2}}{\frac{7}{4}} \\ b & =10\text{ mm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=10\,\text{mm}.$

\begin{aligned}c & =AB=7\sqrt{2}\,\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186105904/plots/c96d0cd3bdc91578941cbc2d6bc33053ecd33e1cc555f6ce78821881cea533f8.png)

The area of ​​the triangle $△ABC$ is $14\sqrt{3}{\text{cm}}^{2}.$ Then,  $AC=${{field-1}} $\text{cm}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The formula for the area of the triangle is 

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}bc\operatorname{sin}⁡A,
$$

where $∠A$ is between the sides of lengths $b$ and $c.$ 

Here

$$
\begin{aligned}c & =AB=7\text{ cm}, \\ b & =AC, \\ m∠A & ={120}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Since 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},
$$

we can calculate $b=AC,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot c\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡A \\ 14\sqrt{3} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{120}^{∘} \\ 14\sqrt{3} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot b\cdot 7\cdot (\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}) \\ 14\sqrt{3} & =\frac{7}{2}b\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 28\cancel{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} & =\frac{7}{2}b\cdot \cancel{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}} \\ \frac{7}{2}b & =28 \\ b & =8\text{ cm}.\end{aligned}
$$

We conclude that $AC=8\,\text{ cm}.$
